scope: Bound template-detail like reconciliation to the confirmed server record

finding.code_evidence: After a successful likeTemplate(target.id), _syncLikeStateAfterToggle called the full-catalog/title-matching helper, retrieving every active template and its document even though the exact server ID had just been confirmed.
change: Pass the exact ID used by the successful mutation into its follow-up.
Use the existing repository.getTemplate(id) single-record query, leaving initial legacy title matching unchanged.
Retain the operation/account/repository guard before the read and after completion. Reject a mismatched ID or retired record.
Keep confirmed optimistic state on read failure, with no full-catalog fallback or retry loop.

after_control.description: The initial catalog hydration is unchanged; each subsequent like reconciliation reads one row.

test_changes: Add a 256-record/five-toggle bound on full versus individual reads and lazy unrelated document generation.
Add failed-read, retired-record and wrong-ID cases that preserve confirmed likes without expanding to a catalog query.
Move existing controlled late responses to the single-record API without removing the stale operation, account switch, close/reopen, initial hydration or rollback assertions.
Strengthen close/account-change/slow-storage tests with explicit assertions that no single-record follow-up starts after their view/owner is no longer current.

checked: The confirmed mutation ID is used instead of mutable widget identity after awaits.
Late older operations and previous-account replies cannot change UI, persistence or list invalidations.
A closed view or changed owner does not begin a follow-up; a previously started read is ignored at completion.
Retired and mismatched records cannot replace the valid local artwork or confirmed like snapshot.
Initial remote title matching, document preparation, edition previews, gallery movement, purchase keys and pricing guards remain unchanged.
No new cache, history, subscription, polling, decoding work per frame or extra document generation was introduced.
The summary-sharing repository, preference write queue, store screen, category strip and prior gallery fixture are byte-for-byte unchanged.
review.shared_workspace: Captured source/test snapshots before editing. Did not swap, revert or clean any shared file. Only the listed source, test and this new verification record were modified for this run.

before.observed_failure: Expected one initial full-catalog read, actual six.

follow_up.completed_previous_candidate: Single-record reconciliation after successful template likes.
next_candidates: Inspect main album and reader hidden/resume image preparation and subscription/cache disposal against newer verification records.
Review idle detail account changes and same-account re-login separately if a reproducible path is found.
The one-record API still includes that book document; consider a metadata-only API only if supported by a demonstrated remaining cost and without weakening retirement checks.

limits: The measured bounds are controlled repository/widget test counts, not production latency, network bytes or native memory measurements.
An already-started read is not physically cancelled. Existing operation/owner guards discard obsolete completions.
Initial legacy hydration still uses the full catalog, and the single-record API still returns one full template document. This change removes the repeated all-catalog reads after confirmed likes.
Real-device frame timing and memory were not profiled. App builds, device execution, deployments and customer data changes were not performed.
